the level of family and school environment perceived by adolescents, as well as their individual characteristics, are associated with school aggression.

the family environment, and the environment at school, influence the individual characteristics of adolescents, which in turn, are related to the development of aggressive behaviour.

the analysis of the relationships among individual characteristics and family and school environments, and their role as antecedents of school aggression.
the analysis of the role of family environment, the classroom environment, individual characteristics and their interrelationships in the explanation of aggressive behaviour in school.
the role of individual and social variables in the development of aggressive behaviour in adolescence.

the family and classroom contexts play a significant role in the development of individual characteristics and aggressive behaviour at school in adolescence.

the family and school contexts are related to the aggressive behaviour at school of adolescents, and that this relationship is mediated by the adolescents' individual characteristics, which are also related to the family and school context.
school aggression in adolescence is a complex and multi-causal process, which requires a more detailed examination of the individual and environmental factors that may influence its development.

the family environment is a significant factor in the explanation of aggressive behaviour in adolescents, although it is not the only factor.
school aggression is the result of an interplay between individual characteristics, family and school environments.
school aggression is the result of the interrelation between individual characteristics and environmental variables.

the family and school contexts are related to the development of individual characteristics that mediate the relationship of the school environment with school aggression in adolescence.
the family context is a key variable to explain the aggressive behaviour of adolescents in school.
